blocks.value: Have you ever heard your parents say, 'Things were much cheaper when we were young'? That is inflation.
Imagine This: A burger cost ₹50 five years ago. Today the same burger costs ₹80. Your money buys fewer burgers than before.
Inflation means the prices of goods and services increase over time. As prices rise, the purchasing power of your money decreases.
If you keep ₹1,000 in a drawer for many years, it will still be ₹1,000. But because prices increase, it may buy fewer things in the future.
This is one of the biggest reasons people invest instead of only saving.
